title: Clo Vendor Leaderboard: Business Impact
description:
We’re officially debuting the CLO Vendor Leaderboard, a platform created to connect brands with the most innovative 3D-ready partners in the industry. This year, we’re spotlighting pioneers across Hong Kong and Southeast Asia: Busana Apparel Group, Cobalt Fashion, Crystal International, GMS+, Hop Lun, Newtimes Group, Daehan Global, PT. Kahatex, and Trax Intertrade.

In the third CLO Vendor Leaderboard video series, Business Impact, we explore how the industry's top vendors turn digital innovation into tangible economic results. Watch as they break down real-world success stories including a 72-hour fast-track timeline, a 45% reduction in sampling costs, and a smart strategy for clearing liability fabric using advanced 3D simulation.

This series covers the 5 essentials of 3D success: 
1️⃣ 3D Capacity 
2️⃣ Investment & Resources 
3️⃣ Business Impact 
4️⃣ Partnership
5️⃣ Strategic Vision

markdown_content: ## 3D Sampling and Digital Fabrication Benefits This section explains how using 3D samples and digital fabric simulations instead of physical prototypes accelerates product development, reduces costs, and improves decision-making accuracy in fashion production. We replaced physical proto-samples with 3D samples created in Glow, digitized fabric textures, simulated fit variations, and shared styles directly with buyers through real-time close-up views. This approach accelerated decision-making, allowing us to skip two rounds of physical samples. As a result, sampling costs were reduced by about 45%, and development timelines shortened from six weeks to four weeks. Buyers approved designs directly from 3D visuals, ensuring the first physical sample was accurate. One client had significant liability fabric stock, which they repurposed into existing styles for outlet stores. To speed up this process, we scanned all fabrics and presented styles virtually in 3D, allowing them to review and approve before moving directly to pre-production (PP) samples and production. This led to a fast and efficient turnaround. ## Fast Track Sampling with CLO and Vue This section covers a rapid product development case study using CLO and Vue software, highlighting dramatic improvements in lead time and sampling accuracy. At the start of the year, we completed a three-day fast-track project with a client using Vue. Traditionally, the sampling to order placement process took 21 days with a 50-60% hit rate for sample approval. With CLO, the entire process was completed in 72 hours, including only eight hours of actual sampling time, achieving a 95% hit rate. This demonstrated the capability to go directly from design to production order without any physical prototypes. ## Virtual Color Collections and 3D Product Visualization This section details how 3D garment modeling and virtual color options reduce physical sampling for seasonal product lines while lowering material and dyeing costs. Each season, the brand introduced a new lace collection with multiple color options. Traditionally, this required numerous physical samples, leading to high material, dyeing costs, and extended timelines. Our solution was a proprietary production product collection using our own fabrics combined with highly detailed 3D garment models. Brands could virtually review color option combinations early in the design process, enabling confident final color selections. This significantly reduced the need for physical samples, saving time, costs, and resources. ## Impact of 3D Workflows on Collaboration and Product Development This section discusses how 3D workflows improve collaboration across time zones, reduce development time, and increase the scale of digital product innovation. 3D sampling has been the most significant improvement in digital product development. It enables real-time collaboration with design teams across multiple time zones, allowing designers to see every iteration immediately. Pattern adjustments, gauge modifications, and multi-style options can be applied digitally without producing physical samples. Before using CLO, this process was slow and dependent on physical sample production. Now, with CLO’s 3D visualization, we can deliver 100% digital product outputs quickly without incurring physical material costs. This shift has expanded the portion of products developed with CLO from covering 10% to 80% of the product range. ## Faster Decision-Making and Accurate Virtual Samples This section highlights how realistic 3D garment simulations with fabric physics accelerate material and color selection, streamline approvals, and reduce development costs. Our 3D workflows enable brands to make quicker decisions on materials and colors through realistic visualization and virtual samples, which allow efficient evaluations and faster approvals. For example, one brand requires all sweater samples to be created in 3D to decide early whether to continue development, significantly reducing time and costs associated with repeated physical sample edits. We simulate accurate fabric physics and share options such as colorways, trims, and fit variations in a single view. This clarity provides buyers immediate understanding and unlocks creativity and customization. ## Pattern Grading and Fit Simulation in 3D This section explains how digital pattern grading and fit simulations reduce errors and miscommunications before physical sampling. Using CLO, we simulate pattern grading across various sizes, allowing brands to track the digital representation of garments accurately before producing physical samples. This detailed digital explanation of fit, design, and construction minimizes the risk of costly miscommunication or errors. Consequently, fewer inaccurate physical samples are made, saving time, cost, and resources. ## Business Impact and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) This section outlines the measurable business benefits of 3D workflows, including cost savings, reduced physical sampling, and faster time-to-market. Our 3D workflow results in a more efficient approval process, shorter development cycles, and increased confidence in final products for partner brands. Key performance indicators tracked include: - Intense reduction in physical samples, replacing 2-3 rounds with 3D approvals - Time-to-market improvements saving days or weeks in development - Cost savings across sampling, courier fees, and manpower - Efficiency per style measured by adoption of 3D assets, with fabrics and templates reused across multiple styles - Increased adoption of 3D samples by buyers, enabling faster digital reviews and approvals These metrics demonstrate clear business value and improve collaboration and client relationships. ## Sustainability and Continuous Improvement with 3D Technology This section covers the sustainability benefits and ongoing value creation achieved through 3D product development technology. Lira prioritizes efficiency and sustainability by using fully fashioned garments that generate less wastage compared to cut-and-sew methods, where leftover fabric for markers is discarded. At HAPEX, we cultivate continuous value with partners by utilizing 3D technology to identify and mitigate physical product errors early through 3D simulations. 3D mockups build trust with partners and accelerate decision-making, reinforcing the advantages of digital product development. --- For more information, visit [www.HAPEX.com](http://www.HAPEX.com).
